jdr.title: Role-Playing Application
jdr.intro1: This role-playing application aims to deliver a complete online tabletop experience, allowing players to join a campaign without being in the same place.
jdr.intro2: It brings together everything needed to play: communication between players, character management, character relationships and story tracking.
jdr.intro3: Instead of relying on separate tools such as Discord for chat, dice apps and external maps, the application brings everything together for a smoother, more immersive experience.
jdr.intro4: It includes a chat system, an information board for tracking relationships between characters, and visibility rules. Each player can see only what their character is meant to know, making the game more realistic.
jdr.intro5: The goal is to make campaign management easier for the game master while giving players a dynamic experience with real-time interactions such as moving tokens on a map and rolling virtual dice.
jdr.done2: Symfony backend with a REST API
jdr.technicalTitle: How It Works and Technical Choices
jdr.technical1: The application has a clear separation between frontend and backend, keeping the code organised and making future development easier.
jdr.technical2: The frontend was built with React to provide a dynamic, responsive interface, especially for player interactions and real-time updates.
jdr.technical3: Symfony powers the backend, structuring the application and handling data, users and game rules through a REST API.
jdr.technical4: This structure keeps the application maintainable and makes it easier to extend with new features.
jdr.security1: Role-based access controls what each user can do and restricts access to sensitive features.
jdr.security2: Actions are checked to prevent unauthorised changes, especially to character data, relationships and campaign progress.
jdr.security3: Communication between the frontend and backend is validated to keep submitted data valid and consistent.
jdr.security4: User authentication uses JWT tokens to secure access and communication within the application.

csharp.title: Content Management Application
csharp.intro1: A placement project at Akira, a company specialising in professional software. The application is designed for funeral-services businesses and centralises information needed for their operations.
csharp.intro2: I had not used C# before this placement. I quickly adapted to the company's environment, learned the technology independently and delivered a complete feature within the deadline.
csharp.intro3: I was asked to build a system for managing directories, pages and topics (rich text content), with a dynamic interface, progressive data loading and real-time synchronisation through SignalR.
csharp.feature1: Full CRUD management for directories, pages and topics
csharp.feature2: Progressive loading and a local cache for topics
csharp.feature4: Keyword search with the full path displayed (Directory / Page / Topic)
csharp.feature6: Role management, with some actions restricted to moderators
csharp.feature7: Dynamic forms with ObjectProxy and a rich-text editor
csharp.architecture1: The application uses a modular architecture with clear separation of responsibilities: a Domain layer for entities, Services for business logic, and Controllers to expose API endpoints.
csharp.architecture2: The PostgreSQL database runs through Docker. Schemas were generated from C# entities with Entity Framework. Code was version-controlled with Git on Azure DevOps, using regular commits with clear messages.
